nodes.content: Develop streaming code-switching speech recognition that generalizes to unseen language pairings without sacrificing monolingual accuracy.
requirements: Reduce WER within three words of switches by 15% relative to a matched multilingual baseline.
Evaluate unseen pairings; keep monolingual WER degradation below 0.5 percentage points at matched streaming latency.

nodes.content: Train a chunkwise transducer with shared phoneme bottlenecks, switch-spliced augmentation, boundary-weighted loss, and frozen-teacher monolingual distillation.
Can shared phoneme bottlenecks and boundary weighting improve switch recognition on unseen pairs without exceeding 0.5-point monolingual WER loss?
Phoneme bottlenecks and boundary weighting reduce unseen-pair switch-window WER ≥15%; distillation holds monolingual WER loss ≤0.5 points at matched latency.

Train English–Spanish/English–Arabic; test held-out Spanish–Arabic against matched baseline, ablating bottlenecks, boundary weighting, distillation; compare switch-window/monolingual WER at fixed latency.
Run SwitchHoldout-v1 ablations on held-out Spanish–Arabic; measure switch-window and monolingual WER against a matched baseline at 320-ms latency.
On held-out Spanish–Arabic, switch-window WER fell 34.0%→28.5% (16.2% relative); monolingual WER rose 12.0%→12.3% at 320-ms latency.
Advance the full model to additional unseen-pair validation: switch-window WER improved 16.2% relative, with 0.3-point monolingual loss.
After advancing the full model, add English–French training; compare French–Arabic/French–Spanish switch-window and monolingual WER with matched baselines at 320-ms latency.
Run SwitchHoldout-v2: add English–French training, then score held-out French–Arabic/French–Spanish switch-window and monolingual WER against matched baselines at 320-ms latency.
SwitchHoldout-v2 report containing unseen-pair switch-window WER, monolingual WER, matched-baseline comparisons, 320-ms latency checks, and training-pair manifests.
Audit SwitchHoldout-v2 report for training-pair leakage; recompute unseen-pair switch-window gains, monolingual WER deltas, and 320-ms latency compliance.
Leakage-free French–Arabic/French–Spanish switch-window WER fell 17.1%/15.6% relative; monolingual WER rose 0.2/0.4 points at 320 ms.
At 320 ms, removing boundary weighting halves unseen-pair switch-window gains, while removing distillation exceeds 0.5-point monolingual WER loss.
Run SwitchHoldout-v2 ablations removing boundary weighting or distillation; compare unseen-pair switch-window gains and monolingual WER at 320-ms latency.
At 320 ms, removing boundary weighting retained 14.8%/13.9% relative unseen-pair switch-window gains; removing distillation caused ≤0.4-point monolingual WER loss.
Bottlenecks drive unseen-pair gains; boundary weighting adds 1–3 points of relative WER reduction; without distillation, monolingual loss remains ≤0.5 points.
On unseen SwitchHoldout-v2 pairs, ablate bottlenecks and verify boundary-weighting gains and no-distillation monolingual WER at 320-ms latency.
Removing phoneme bottlenecks preserved 16.0%/15.1% relative switch-window WER gains on French–Arabic/French–Spanish versus matched baselines at 320 ms.
Switch-spliced augmentation drives ≥15% unseen-pair switch-window WER gains without bottlenecks; distillation limits monolingual loss to ≤0.5 points across four languages.
Independently ablate switch-spliced augmentation and distillation without bottlenecks; compare three unseen-pair switch-window WERs and four monolingual WERs at 320 ms.
At 320 ms, removing switch-spliced augmentation retained 15.4%/15.2%/15.0% switch-window WER gains on Spanish–Arabic/French–Arabic/French–Spanish.
Boundary-weighted loss and distillation alone sustain ≥15% unseen-pair switch-window WER gains and ≤0.5-point monolingual losses without bottlenecks or splice augmentation.
Measure switch-window/monolingual WER for the boundary-weighted, distilled transducer without bottlenecks/splicing across three unseen pairs and four languages at 320 ms.
Without bottlenecks or splicing, Spanish–Arabic/French–Arabic/French–Spanish switch-window WER gains fell to 12.8%/13.1%/11.9%; monolingual losses stayed ≤0.4 points at 320 ms.
Replicate the bottleneck-free, splice-free model across five seeds on speaker-disjoint SwitchHoldout-v3; test ≥15% gains and ≤0.5-point losses at 320 ms.
On SwitchHoldout-v3, five-seed means showed ≥15.1% switch-window WER gains across three unseen pairs and ≤0.4-point monolingual losses at 320 ms.
On speaker-disjoint SwitchHoldout-v3, boundary-weighted, distilled models without bottlenecks/splicing achieve ≥15% mean unseen-pair switch-window WER gains and ≤0.5-point monolingual loss.
Extend training with English–Italian; test streamlined model on speaker-disjoint Italian–Arabic/Italian–Spanish with five-seed confidence intervals and monolingual WER at 320 ms.
Retrain with English–Italian; rerun five-seed SwitchHoldout-v3 switch-window/monolingual WER, then test Italian–Arabic/Italian–Spanish against matched baselines at 320 ms.
SwitchHoldout-v3 five-seed means: five unseen pairs cut switch-window WER ≥15% relative (Italian–Arabic/Italian–Spanish: 15.8%/15.3%); monolingual losses ≤0.4 points at 320 ms.
Advance the streamlined model to external validation, not deployment: SwitchHoldout-v3 meets targets, but earlier v2 missed switch-gain targets.
Use confidence-gated articulatory adapters with switch-triggered token rescoring, bypassing adapters on confident monolingual spans at 320-ms latency.
Can confidence gating activate articulatory rescoring near unseen-pair switches without false triggers that raise monolingual WER?
Entropy-gated articulatory rescoring reduces unseen-pair switch-window WER ≥15%, with <5% monolingual false-trigger rate and <0.5-point WER loss at 320 ms.
Train entropy-gated articulatory adapters; on SwitchHoldout-v3, measure unseen-pair switch-window WER and monolingual false-trigger rate/WER versus matched baseline at 320 ms.
SwitchHoldout-v3: unseen-pair switch-window WER fell 17% relative; monolingual false triggers reached 9%, raising WER 0.7 points at 320 ms.
Two-chunk hysteresis plus articulatory confirmation retain ≥15% unseen-pair switch-window WER gains with <5% false triggers and ≤0.5-point monolingual loss.
Benchmark two-chunk hysteresis and articulatory confirmation on SwitchHoldout-v3; compare unseen-pair switch-window WER, false triggers, monolingual WER at 320 ms.
SwitchHoldout-v3: hysteresis-confirmed rescoring reduced unseen-pair switch-window WER 15.6% relative; monolingual false triggers 3.8%, WER loss 0.3 points at 320 ms.
Compose independently trained language-specific subword heads in a streaming transducer with calibrated switch priors and reserved monolingual beam paths.
Can calibrated priors prevent unseen-pair switch-token pruning while reserved beams limit monolingual WER loss to 0.5 points?
Train English, Spanish, Arabic, French heads separately; calibrate switch priors on seen pairs, then benchmark held-out Spanish–Arabic/French–Arabic at 320 ms.
Train four language-specific heads; tune switch priors on English–Spanish/English–Arabic, then score unseen Spanish–Arabic/French–Arabic against a matched 320-ms baseline.
HeadCompose-v1 bundle containing four language heads, seen-pair-calibrated switch priors, reserved-beam decoder, and unseen-pair WER benchmarks at 320 ms.
Ablate HeadCompose-v1 priors and reserved beams; measure unseen-pair switch-token pruning, switch-window WER, and monolingual WER at 320 ms.
HeadCompose-v1 priors halved switch-token pruning; unseen-pair switch-window WER fell 16% relative, and reserved beams cut monolingual loss 0.8→0.3 points.
Select HeadCompose-v1 for external validation: three approaches meet WER thresholds, but modular language heads offer simpler unseen-pair composition.
